title: Seed Node Operator & Rack-Aware PXE Fallback Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a practical pattern we've prototyped for on-prem cluster bootstrap where a lightweight 'seed node operator' automates initial cluster assembly, and the PXE bootstrap flow includes an iPXE fallback path for mixed-rack hardware. The goal is to reduce manual intervention for first-boot operations and make rolling upgrades and recovery deterministic across bare metal and vSphere-managed edge racks.

Scope & assumptions:
- Targets: small-to-medium on-prem clusters (3–24 nodes) across bare metal racks and vSphere-hosted blades.
- Network: L2 broadcast for PXE across rack leaf; DHCP + TFTP on bootstrap VLAN; separate management VLAN for cluster traffic.
- PKI: Root CA and vault are accessible from seed nodes during bootstrap.
- Storage: local disk for kubelet + optional remote PV via CSI.
- Team: SRE + platform engineer operate bootstrap infra; solution can be adapted by field eng.

High level flow:
1. Rack power-on -> DHCP assigns IP and boots iPXE from NIC ROM.
2. iPXE attempts netboot chain to local TFTP/HTTP server. If server unreachable, iPXE executes fallback script to download a tiny busybox initramfs from the CDN.
3. Busybox initramfs mounts ephemeral RAM root, contacts bootstrap metadata service (HTTP) with rack-id and MAC list.
4. Bootstrap service schedules the node to a seed node pool (label by rack), returns terraform-ignition blob + cloud-init overlay.
5. Node applies ignition, installs container runtime, joins the seed operator-controlled bootstrap cluster.
6. Seed operator provisions remaining control-plane and worker nodes via kubeadm + kubelet config, and finally issues certificates and lifecycle hooks for full production cluster.

Key design notes:
- Seed operator: lightweight controller running as a static pod on 3 seed nodes. Responsibilities: orchestrate kubeadm init/join sequences, publish per-node ignition fragments, manage preflight checks, and coordinate TLS bootstrap tokens with short TTLs.
- Rack-awareness: nodes present a rack label (from DHCP option 43 or metadata server). Seed operator uses this to place control-plane pads across racks for fault domains.
- PXE fallback: iPXE first tries local HTTP; if unavailable, falls back to signed initramfs from global CDN that can reach bootstrap service across routed mgmt networks. This reduces onsite tech trips when TFTP is misconfigured.

Terraform module notes (recommended module split):
1) module.hardware_inventory (inputs: rack_id, mac_addresses, bmc_endpoints; outputs: node_ids, reserved_ips) -- manages static inventory and IP reservations.
2) module.pxe_infra (inputs: dhcp_range, tftp_image_repo, http_boot_endpoint) -- creates DHCP/TFTP config templates, systemd service units for tftp/http.
3) module.seed_operator (inputs: seed_count, tls_ca_secret_ref, gitops_repo) -- bootstraps seed operator manifests, bootstrap-configs stored in S3-compatible backend.
4) module.networking (inputs: mgmt_cidr, pod_cidr, service_cidr) -- allocates subnets and fabric ACLs for initial bootstrap stage.
Notes: split inventory from infra so field techs can run inventory refresh without touching PXE configs. Use idempotent templates and small state files per-rack.

Upgrade plan (rolling kernel + container runtime + k8s control plane):
- Versioning strategy: follow +1 minor for kubeadm/kubelet with conservative window; prefer 3-node control plane for easier quorum.
- Pre-upgrade checks: node readiness, time sync, disk pressure, kubelet logs for CRI errors. Run "/opt/internal/bin/preflight-checks.sh --level=critical".
- Step 0: take cluster snapshot (etcd snapshot + object store sync).
- Step 1: upgrade seed operator to v1.x to add cordon-aware draining hooks.
- Step 2: drain and upgrade control-plane nodes sequentially (safe failover): kubeadm upgrade apply <target>; verify apiserver metrics and endpoints.
- Step 3: upgrade kubelets on workers with surge 1 at a time using machine annotate to prevent simultaneous concurrency across racks.
- Rollback: keep the old kubeadm artifact in /opt/rollback; if control-plane fails to reach quorum, restore etcd snapshot and reapply previous manifests.

Verification playbook (post-upgrade):
- smoke: kubectl get nodes (STATUS Ready), kubectl get cs, check core-dns and ingress pods restart counts.
- perf: run 3-mtps tokenized generation scenario using local load-client to validate P99 latencies.
- security: run image-scan on freshly-pulled images and validate pod security admission logs.

Troubleshooting common failures:
- PXE image not served: verify tftpd-hpa status, check firewall between leaf and tftp host; test iPXE fallback URL by manually requesting initramfs.
- Seed operator stuck in CrashLoop: check hostPath volumes for kubeadm logs, ensure CA password is accessible in vault.
- Node flaps after ignition: inspect systemd-journald for dracut or initramfs network mount issues; confirm MTU mismatch across switch stack.

Runbook snippets (copyable commands):
- Force rebootstrap a node: ssh bmc && ipmitool chassis power cycle; wait 45s; tail -f /var/log/pxe/boot.log | grep <MAC>.
- Generate ignition fragment: ./tools/gen-ignition --node-id node-42 --rack r3 > /var/tmp/node-42.ign
- Take etcd snapshot (seed control-plane): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 snapshot save /tmp/etcd-backup.db --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt

Operational recommendations:
- Keep seed operator image small (<60MB compressed) and signed.
- Maintain a minimal offline fallback artifact set on USB for field operations (ignition templates, signed initramfs, small help.html).
- Automate post-bootstrap health checks and emit Slack alerts into #infra-ops with machine-readable payloads.
- Maintain a per-rack terraform state bucket to reduce blast radius of accidental state changes.

Outstanding questions & TODOs:
- Decide on BMC credential rotation cadence and store schema (vault path vs HSM).
- Evaluate rate limiting on bootstrap service to avoid thundering herd on large rack power-cycles.
- Field test iPXE fallback with three carrier switches that perform VLAN pruning.

Appendix: useful links and templates
- sample iPXE fallback script (in repo infra/pxe/fallback.ipxe)
- terraform module prototypes (infra/modules/{hardware_inventory,pxe_infra,seed_operator})
- emergency rollback checklist (confluence:private-deployments/rollback)

Last notes: treat this as a living doc; the next iteration should capture concrete metrics from field trials (time-to-cluster-ready, median bootstrap time per rack) and a short runbook for onboarding new field engineers.
